subject: Supplemental controls and split of responsibilities for DPA (Art.28/30)
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@atlasbank.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: DPA clarifications — subprocessors / Art.28 responsibilities

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the intro call earlier. Before we proceed with onboarding, Legal & InfoSec have a few open items on the DPA and subprocessor split of responsibility that we need clarified so our internal DPIA and procurement can move forward: 

- Which subprocessors will process EU personal data (list + location)?
- For any subprocessors outside the EEA, what transfer mechanisms are in place (SCCs, adequacy, encryption-in-flight/end)?
- We need an annotated Art.30-style processing register or equivalent export for our DPIA team (fields we need: processing purpose, categories, location, retention, legal basis).
- Audit rights: are you able to provide timeboxed access to operational logs and a point-in-time export for a third-party auditor? If so, what scope/SLAs do you propose?
- KMS & keywrap: do you support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) or double-wrap models?

Can you send any sample evidence (architecture diagram, Art.30 extract, sample DPIA notes) ahead of a short workshop? We aim to have procurement sign-off within two weeks, so any quick turnarounds would help.

Best,
Maria
Maria Gomez
Procurement Lead, AtlasBank
security@atlasbank.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@atlasbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications — subprocessors / Art.28 responsibilities

Hi Maria,

Thanks — appreciate the clear list. I pulled together a short package that should address most of the items and will set up a workshop to walk the DPIA and InfoSec teams through the specifics. Highlights below and attachments (see list at the end):

- Subprocessors: attached workbook (subprocessor-responsibility-split.xlsx) lists the current production subprocessors, primary region, and which roles they perform (storage, telemetry, infra ops, logging). Columns include data residency (EEA/US/APAC) and whether EEA personal data is processed. Note: we perform regular subprocessors reviews and will notify 30 days prior to any change per the DPA.
- Transfers: for subprocessors outside the EEA we use SCCs + contractual safeguards; for certain cloud-hosted storage we additionally enable encryption at rest and in transit. Where customers require, we support regional deployment pinning to an EEA-only cluster.
- Art.30 / DPIA evidence: attached a one-page Art.30 extract and an annotated DPIA sample (redacted). If you need a different extract format, tell us which fields and we'll export a CSV.
- Audit rights: we can support timeboxed read-only access to operational logs and provide a point-in-time export (redacted) for an accredited auditor. Suggested scope: uptime/incident logs, access logs, configuration snapshots for the last 90 days. We propose a 5-business-day turnaround for the export and a signed NDA for the auditor.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys via partner KMS integrations (AWS KMS/CloudHSM, GCP CMEK) for select dedicated and private deployments; for hosted customers we offer envelope key management with customer key wrap in enterprise add-ons.

Next steps I propose: 1) quick internal review of the attached supplements, 2) a 60-minute workshop next week with your DPIA/InfoSec/legal to walk the artifacts, and 3) agree redlines for the DPA addendum.

Attachments (stubs): DPA_Supplemental_Controls_v1.pdf, subprocessor-responsibility-split.xlsx, dpia-sample-annotated.pdf

If you want, I can loop in Legal for a quick redline call — Ben has a few suggested edits.

Cheers,
Vivek
Head of Trust & Safety Operations
Redwood Inference

--

Subject: Re: DPA clarifications — subprocessors / Art.28 responsibilities

Vivek / team,

Looping in a few commercial/legal pointers based on AtlasBank's asks — quick summary of proposed redlines (attached as redline-proposal.docx):

- Audit rights: carve a narrow, time-limited operational audit option: 1) customer auditor scope limited to infrastructure configuration and access logs (no source code review), 2) redacted PII in exports unless otherwise agreed, 3) company contact and 10 business days' notice.
- Retention & deletion: add a clause that we will provide a retention/export snapshot at termination and hold exports for 30 days for retrieval.
- Subprocessor notifications: increase notification window to 30 days and provide the option for an "onshore replacement" where feasible.
- KMS / keywrap: propose offering an enterprise toggle for CMEK in Dedicated + Private only; for Hosted, envelope-key with customer wrap and audit logs will be the default.

I've attached a draft redline to accelerate the legal exchange. Also flagged a HubSpot ticket for procurement follow-up: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/contact/DB-Atlas-2027-042 (internal reference).

Ben
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
